sources.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), full author text
sources.locator: Full author text, Sections 2.1 (Kernel Interpolants, equations (1)–(7)); 2.2 (Variational Derivation, fixed/adaptive smoothing discussion, equations (12)–(25) and conservation discussion); and 5.7 (The Tensile Instability, pp. 419–420). Those complete subsections and the full derivation paragraphs cited here were inspected.

contents.name: §2.1 Kernel Interpolants: normalized symmetric C² kernels, compact support, convolution smoothing and kernel-sum density estimate
contents.proof_mapping: The item fixes a nonnegative radial fixed-width family; second-order bias and its moment proof are supplied locally in thm-second-order-meshfree-convolution-bias.

contents.name: §2.1 Kernel Interpolants: particle summation approximation and the finite-neighbor sampling limitation
contents.proof_mapping: The item gives the exact cellwise oscillation sum and the h/ε and h/ε² bounds; it does not import an unstated neighbor-limit claim.

contents.name: §2.2 Variational Derivation: symmetric pressure-gradient force and the matched thermal-energy equation
contents.proof_mapping: The fixed-width formula is authored locally with the exact matched energy equation. Springel’s adaptive-smoothing formulation includes grad-h correction factors, which this fixed-ε page does not import.

contents.name: §2.2 Variational Derivation: linear momentum, angular momentum and energy conservation from the discrete symmetries
contents.proof_mapping: The local proof groups the actual pair forces and uses antisymmetry and radial centrality.

contents.name: §5.7 The Tensile Instability: a close-pair gap can shrink under the surrounding pressure forces and particles can clump
contents.proof_mapping: The local three-particle witness computes the exact initial relative acceleration and separately verifies conservation.

sources.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)
sources.locator: Complete six-page Lecture 25 PDF, especially pp. 2–5: non-equidistant particles and meshfree approximation; SPH kernel sequence and convolution; point-cloud quadrature; and the displayed SPH approximation to Euler momentum and energy equations. All six pages were read.

contents.name: p. 2: non-equidistant particle locations and the need for derivative approximations
contents.proof_mapping: The cell rule defines the fill radius, cell weights, and local-volume condition explicitly.

contents.name: p. 3: moving-least-squares meshfree approximation and SPH kernel interpolation
p. 3: compact-support kernels and the continuous smoothing integral
p. 4: discrete point-cloud quadrature of the density-weighted kernel integral
pp. 4–5: symmetrized SPH pressure force and internal-energy equation
pp. 4–5: particle formulation of compressible-flow equations
contents.reason: The page proves finite regularized ODE and kernel-quadrature results only; it makes no continuum Euler shock or singular-limit convergence claim.
